title: Small language models are quietly taking over everyday phone tasks
summary: Device makers are shipping compact models that run fully on-device, cutting latency and cloud costs. Early benchmarks suggest they handle most summarising and drafting jobs well.

title: Regulators draft first rules for AI systems used in hiring
summary: A new proposal would require employers to disclose when automated tools screen candidates. Industry groups say the audit requirements are vague and costly.

title: Why AI coding assistants still struggle with large legacy codebases
summary: Engineers report that assistants excel at new files but lose track of decades of implicit conventions. Teams are responding with better repository indexing and written style guides.

title: Chipmakers race to cut the power draw of data-center accelerators
summary: Electricity is becoming the main constraint on training clusters. New designs trade peak speed for efficiency per watt.

title: Researchers show a new way to make chatbots admit when they do not know
summary: A calibration technique lets models flag low-confidence answers without hurting accuracy. The authors say it could reduce confident but wrong responses in medical and legal tools.

title: A decade on, Rust adoption reaches mainstream infrastructure teams
summary: More companies are rewriting performance-critical services in Rust, citing memory safety. Hiring remains the main obstacle.

title: The case for boring technology in small engineering teams
summary: A veteran engineer argues that choosing well-understood tools frees time for product work. Novelty, she says, should be rationed like a budget.

title: Open source maintainers weigh new funding models after burnout survey
summary: A survey finds most maintainers work unpaid and consider quitting. Sponsorship programmes help a few projects but leave the long tail exposed.

title: Phishing kits now imitate bank apps with near-perfect pixel accuracy
summary: Analysts say new kits copy login flows so well that visual checks no longer help. Hardware security keys remain effective against them.

title: A routine software update closed a flaw affecting millions of routers
summary: Vendors urge owners to install the patch, as attackers had begun scanning for exposed devices. Many home routers update only when users act.

title: Ransomware gangs shift to stealing data instead of encrypting it
summary: Incident responders see more extortion without lockouts, which makes backups less useful. Defenders are focusing on limiting what attackers can copy.

title: Seed investors grow pickier as founders return to profitability targets
summary: Early-stage funds report more questions about unit economics and fewer about growth at any cost. Smaller rounds are becoming common.

title: Karachi founders build a logistics startup around neighbourhood shops
summary: The company routes small deliveries through existing kiryana stores to cut last-mile costs. It plans to expand to three more cities this year.

title: What a failed startup taught its founder about hiring too early
summary: In a candid post-mortem, the founder says payroll outran learning. The advice: stay small until customers pull you forward.

title: Accelerator demo days look different in a quieter funding climate
summary: Investors now ask about customers and cash runway first, and the pitch second. Founders say the shift rewards clear thinking.

title: Benchmark index edges higher as investors await earnings season
summary: Trading was thin with energy and banking shares leading gains. Analysts expect guidance, not results, to move prices.

title: Bond yields ease as inflation data comes in softer than forecast
summary: Lower yields lifted rate-sensitive stocks. Strategists caution that one report does not make a trend.

title: Retail investors pile into index funds for the long haul
summary: Fund flow data shows steady monthly buying regardless of headlines. Advisers say consistency matters more than timing.

title: Why dividend stocks are back in fashion with cautious savers
summary: Steady payouts look attractive as growth stocks swing. Analysts warn about chasing high yields without checking cash flow.

title: Rupee holds steady as remittance inflows stay strong
summary: Overseas transfers continued to support the external account this month. Economists say the cushion depends on exchange-rate stability.

title: Budget talks focus on widening the tax net without hurting salaried earners
summary: Officials are weighing property and retail measures to raise revenue. Business groups ask for predictable rules.

title: Exporters ask for cheaper power to stay competitive
summary: Textile and leather exporters say energy costs erode thin margins. The government is reviewing a targeted tariff.

title: Inflation cools for the third month, central bank watching closely
summary: Food prices eased while utility costs remained elevated. Analysts debate how soon policy rates can fall.

title: Retailers rethink inventory after a year of unpredictable demand
summary: Chains are ordering smaller batches more often to avoid markdowns. Suppliers say the shift pushes costs upstream.

title: Family-run manufacturers adopt software to survive tighter margins
summary: Simple inventory and billing tools are helping owners spot waste. Adoption is slow but steady.

title: Supply-chain managers diversify ports after repeated shipping delays
summary: Companies now route cargo through several hubs to reduce single points of failure. The cost is higher but delays have dropped.

title: Rooftop solar boom reshapes electricity demand on the national grid
summary: Households installing panels are cutting daytime consumption, leaving utilities with unusual evening peaks. Planners are studying storage.

title: Oil prices drift as producers signal steady output
summary: Traders weighed inventory data against cautious demand forecasts. Refiners expect a calm quarter.

title: Battery storage projects move from pilots to procurement
summary: Utilities are tendering grid-scale batteries to smooth renewable output. Costs have fallen sharply over five years.

title: Heatwave season arrives earlier, testing city cooling plans
summary: Municipal planners are adding shade, water points and cool roofs. Health officials urge outdoor workers to adjust schedules.

title: Farmers adopt drought-tolerant seed as rainfall patterns shift
summary: Agronomists say new varieties can hold yields with less water. Access to credit remains the main barrier.

title: Coastal cities weigh mangrove restoration as a low-cost flood defence
summary: Restored mangroves reduce storm surge and support fisheries. Projects need years of community stewardship to succeed.

title: Assembly session opens with debate on provincial funding formula
summary: Lawmakers traded proposals on dividing federal revenue. Observers expect negotiations to continue for weeks.

title: Court asks for clearer timelines in a long-running public land case
summary: The bench urged agencies to file complete records at the next hearing. Residents say delays have stalled local projects.

title: Local government reform returns to the policy agenda
summary: Analysts argue that empowered councils could improve service delivery. Parties disagree on how much authority to devolve.

title: Parliamentary committees quietly shape most of the year's legislation
summary: A review finds that committee amendments change many bills before they reach the floor. Transparency groups want public minutes.

title: Regional talks resume as mediators propose a phased ceasefire
summary: Negotiators described the discussions as constructive but fragile. Humanitarian groups are pressing for aid corridors.

title: Trade corridors become the new diplomacy between neighbouring states
summary: Governments are using customs and transit deals to build ties. Analysts say economic links can calm political friction.

title: A summit's quiet outcome: agreement to keep talking
summary: Leaders left without a joint declaration but scheduled follow-up meetings. Diplomats called that a small success.

title: Opener's unbeaten century puts the home side in control of the Test
summary: A patient innings anchored a total that tested the visiting attack all day. The pitch is expected to turn on day four.

title: Selectors name a young fast bowler in the squad for the T20 series
summary: The 20-year-old impressed in domestic cricket with pace and a late swing. Captains praised the selection's balance.

title: How spin is reshaping the new-ball overs in modern T20
summary: Teams increasingly open with a spinner to stall the powerplay. Data shows it cuts boundary rates against left-handers.

title: Women's league announces a longer season with more home matches
summary: Organisers say the schedule will give players steadier workloads. Broadcasters have agreed to cover every game.

title: Grassroots coaches argue for more turf pitches in small cities
summary: Players trained on concrete often struggle on bouncier surfaces. A pilot programme will lay five new grounds.

title: Retiring captain reflects on two decades of dressing-room change
summary: He recalled how fitness, analytics and mental-health support transformed team culture. His advice to youngsters: stay curious.

title: Title race tightens after a late winner in the weekend's big match
summary: A stoppage-time goal separated two sides who had traded the lead twice. Managers praised the intensity.

title: Clubs experiment with smaller academy squads to speed development
summary: Coaches say fewer players receive more minutes and personal attention. Critics worry about missing late bloomers.

title: The data behind the modern high press
summary: Analysts show how pressing triggers have become more selective. Teams now press in short bursts rather than for 90 minutes.

title: Qualifying shake-up: rookie takes pole in a wet session
summary: Changing conditions rewarded bold tyre calls. The champion starts fourth after a late error.

title: Teams debate next season's rules as budget caps tighten
summary: Engineers say aerodynamic changes could reshape the pecking order. Smaller teams want a fairer share of testing.

title: Inside the pit wall: how strategists decide when to stop
summary: A strategist explains the models used to weigh track position against tyre wear. Human judgement still breaks ties.

title: Large study links regular walking to lower risk of heart disease
summary: Researchers followed participants for ten years and found benefits even at modest step counts. Doctors say consistency counts most.

title: Hospitals trial AI note-taking to give clinicians time back
summary: Early pilots show doctors spending less time on paperwork. Privacy teams are reviewing how recordings are stored.

title: What sleep researchers wish everyone knew about late-night screens
summary: Experts say light matters but so does mental stimulation. Simple evening routines beat gadgets and supplements.

title: Physicists measure a tiny effect that could test a long-standing theory
summary: The experiment used ultra-cold atoms to detect a faint shift. Results will need independent replication.

title: Deep-sea expedition catalogues dozens of unfamiliar species
summary: The team's cameras recorded unusual jellyfish and bottom-dwelling fish. Samples will be sequenced over the coming months.

title: Why replication projects are changing how labs publish
summary: Journals are rewarding careful confirmation as well as novelty. Researchers say the culture is shifting slowly.

title: Lunar lander mission sets a landing date after final tests
summary: Engineers completed fuel and navigation checks this week. The craft will carry instruments to study dust near the south pole.

title: Amateur astronomers help confirm a faint new comet
summary: Backyard telescopes captured the object's motion over several nights. Professionals will refine its orbit.

title: Small satellites make Earth observation affordable for new countries
summary: Compact imaging satellites are letting agencies track crops and floods. Launch rideshares have lowered the entry cost.

title: Universities redesign first-year courses around projects, not lectures
summary: Faculty say project work improves retention and teamwork. Assessment remains the hardest part to reform.

title: Scholarship programme expands to cover rural students
summary: The fund will pay tuition and living costs for several hundred students. Applications open next month.

title: Why exam stress is pushing schools to rethink homework
summary: Counsellors report rising anxiety before board exams. Some schools are trimming homework and adding study skills sessions.

title: Designers revisit typography as screens get larger and calmer
summary: Generous line spacing and serif body text are returning to reading apps. Designers say reading comfort drives retention.

title: Accessibility testing moves earlier in the product cycle
summary: Teams that prototype with screen readers catch problems before engineering begins. Costs fall as a result.

title: Interfaces that end: the case against infinite scroll
summary: Researchers argue that finite lists respect attention and improve satisfaction. Some products now add natural stopping points.

title: Debut novel on a Lahore family wins praise for quiet precision
summary: Reviewers admire its small domestic scenes and understated humour. The author wrote it over six years of early mornings.

title: Essay collections are having a moment among younger readers
summary: Booksellers report brisk sales of personal essays. Readers say short pieces fit busy schedules.

title: The slow pleasure of rereading a favourite book
summary: A critic argues that rereading shows how much of a book lives in the reader. She suggests choosing one title each year.

title: Festival jury praises a low-budget drama shot in a single week
summary: Critics noted the film's patient camera and non-professional cast. It will screen in cinemas next month.

title: Independent musicians turn to subscription fan clubs
summary: Artists say small recurring support is more stable than streaming royalties. Platforms are courting them.

title: Why long-running series are shrinking their seasons
summary: Shorter runs mean tighter stories and fewer filler episodes. Viewers say they finish more shows.

title: Old-city walking tours help residents rediscover their neighbourhoods
summary: Volunteer guides share stories of bazaars, havelis and craft traditions. Tours sell out within hours.

title: Craft fairs return, with makers selling directly online
summary: Handmade jewellery, textiles and ceramics drew steady crowds. Many makers now take orders through social media.

title: The quiet revival of community libraries
summary: Volunteers are turning spare rooms into lending libraries. Donations of children's books are in highest demand.

title: Northern valleys prepare for a record tourist season
summary: Guesthouses are upgrading facilities and road crews are clearing passes. Officials urge visitors to check weather alerts.

title: Airlines add direct routes to secondary cities
summary: Regional airports expect more traffic as carriers test point-to-point flights. Fares may fall on busy routes.

title: Slow travel: spending a week in one place
summary: Travellers report lower costs and deeper experiences when they stay put. Tour operators are building longer itineraries.

title: Regulators sketch a licensing framework for digital asset platforms
summary: The draft sets capital and custody rules for exchanges. Industry groups welcome clarity but dispute the fees.

title: Mobile wallets push digital payments into small-town markets
summary: Shopkeepers say QR payments reduce cash handling. Fraud awareness campaigns accompany the rollout.

title: Stablecoins find a niche in cross-border freelancer payments
summary: Freelancers use them to avoid slow bank transfers. Tax treatment remains unclear in many countries.

title: SBP keeps policy rate at 12pc as inflation expectations anchor
summary: The State Bank of Pakistan held its benchmark rate steady, citing easing core inflation and a stabilising rupee. Analysts say a cut is possible in the next quarter if food prices cooperate.

title: Remittances hit record $3.2bn in June, IMF notes progress
summary: Inflows from the Pakistani diaspora surged to a monthly record, helping the current account swing to a narrow surplus. The IMF praised the improvement as evidence that reforms are working.

title: SIFC fast-tracks 14 industrial projects worth $4bn
summary: The Special Investment Facilitation Council has approved twelve manufacturing and four energy projects. Officials say land acquisition and regulatory approvals have been condensed from years to months.

title: ECP orders re-count in two disputed National Assembly seats
summary: The Election Commission has directed district returning officers to conduct manual tallies after petitions alleged systematic undercounting. Both seats are in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

title: Senate passes digital rights bill after late-night amendments
summary: Lawmakers passed a bill protecting online expression with caveats for national security. Critics say three exception clauses leave too much discretion with the interior ministry.

title: Anthropic releases interpretability map of Claude thought process
summary: Researchers published a study showing which internal features activate when Claude reasons through multi-step problems. The transparency report is the most detailed yet from a frontier lab.

title: Startup raises $120m to bring local-language AI to South Asia
summary: The company claims its Urdu, Bengali and Hindi models outperform GPT-4 on colloquial text by a wide margin. The Series B was led by a Singapore sovereign fund.

title: AI agents write more than half of code at two big tech firms
summary: Internal memos from two FAANG-tier companies show agent-generated code now exceeds 50 percent of commits. Human review is still required but the bottleneck has shifted from writing to reading.

title: Karachi launches AI-powered traffic management pilot on Shahrah-e-Faisal
summary: Cameras and real-time signal control cut average journey times by 18 percent in the first month. The system is built on open-source models fine-tuned on local driving patterns.

title: Pakistan banks urged to patch critical ATM firmware by month-end
summary: The SBP issued an emergency circular after researchers found a buffer overflow in firmware shipped with a popular ATM model. Banks have 30 days to apply vendor patches or take machines offline.

title: Ransomware group claims breach of South Asian telco, leaks call records
summary: A group called DarkPulse posted a sample of metadata from what it says is a mid-size carrier. The telco has not confirmed the breach but has taken systems offline for investigation.

title: Karachi fintech Abhi closes $18m Series A to expand earned-wage access
summary: The startup lets workers withdraw accrued salary before payday for a small fee. The round was led by Vostok Emerging Finance and will fund a push into Lahore and Faisalabad.

title: Y Combinator summer batch has highest-ever ratio of AI infrastructure companies
summary: Sixty percent of the 220 companies in the latest cohort are building developer tooling or model infrastructure. Founder backgrounds shifted toward research scientists and ex-big-lab engineers.

title: PSX KSE-100 breaks 90,000 for first time as foreign inflows return
summary: The benchmark crossed the milestone on strong buying in banking and cement. Foreign portfolio investors bought a net $48m in the week, the most since 2021.

title: Gold hits new record above $3,400 as dollar weakens on Fed signals
summary: Bullion rose 1.4 percent after Fed minutes showed policymakers discussed a July cut. Emerging market central banks continued to be net buyers, led by the People Bank of China.

title: Pakistan to add 1.2GW of solar capacity this year, beating target
summary: Rooftop installations and two utility-scale parks pushed total solar capacity past expectations. Net metering registrations grew 40 percent year-on-year, straining grid balancing.

title: OPEC+ output cut extended as Brent stays below comfort zone
summary: Producers agreed to maintain current reductions through March, frustrating members with fiscal break-evens above market prices. Oil slipped 0.8 percent on concerns about demand from China.

title: Pakistan beat India by 6 wickets in Asia Cup thriller at Lahore
summary: A brilliant 87 not out by Fakhar Zaman carried Pakistan home with two balls to spare. The win puts Pakistan top of Group A and eases pressure on head coach ahead of the World Cup.

title: Nida Dar breaks record for most ODI wickets by a Pakistan woman
summary: The off-spinner claimed her 150th wicket in the series against Sri Lanka, surpassing a mark that had stood for a decade. She also has 1,200 runs, making her the format all-rounder benchmark.

title: Babar Azam T20I average climbs back above 50 after five-match blitz
summary: The captain hit three fifties in a row against New Zealand to recover form that had dipped mid-season. Selectors named an unchanged squad for the upcoming home series against South Africa.

title: Real Madrid sign Bellingham extension through 2030 amid Saudi interest
summary: The England midfielder has committed his future to Madrid after a second successive La Liga title. The club rejected a reported 250m pound offer from an unnamed Saudi club last month.

title: Verstappen takes pole in Monza as Ferrari falter on strategy
summary: The champion qualified on the front row after Ferrari mistimed a late slipstream run. Leclerc will start third after a penalty for impeding Hamilton in Q3.

title: WHO approves first malaria vaccine for children under five
summary: The R21 shot showed 75 percent efficacy in sub-Saharan Africa trials and is cheaper to manufacture than its predecessor. Roll-out starts in Nigeria and Ghana next quarter.

title: Pakistan dengue cases triple in Sindh as monsoon peaks
summary: Hospitals in Karachi and Hyderabad have reported over 4,000 cases this week, exceeding last year full-season total. The provincial health department is deploying rapid-test kits and fogging teams.

title: CERN detects evidence of a new force-carrying particle
summary: Physicists report a 4.8-sigma excess in collision data that could hint at a boson beyond the Standard Model. Independent replication runs are scheduled at three other facilities.

title: Quantum startup achieves 1,000-qubit milestone on room-temperature chip
summary: The team ditched superconducting qubits for a photonic architecture that runs at 25 degrees Celsius. Error rates are still high but the approach sidesteps the expensive cryogenic cooling barrier.

title: NASA Artemis III Moon landing delayed to 2027 after SpaceX suit issues
summary: Engineers need more time to certify the pressure suit for lunar surface operations. The delay pushes back the first woman on the Moon by at least 14 months.

title: Pakistan floods displaced 800,000 last month, more rain forecast
summary: The National Disaster Management Authority says the Indus has breached its banks in four districts. Meteorologists expect above-normal rainfall through September due to a stronger La Nina.

title: Global CO2 concentration hits 430ppm, fastest annual rise on record
summary: Atmospheric monitoring stations confirmed the figure, driven by a combination of fossil-fuel emissions and reduced ocean uptake. Scientists say the 1.5 degree budget will be exhausted within a decade.

title: Pakistan and China sign upgraded CPEC Phase II framework
summary: The two governments expanded the corridor agreement to include digital infrastructure and agriculture. Pakistani officials say the new terms improve revenue sharing on existing power projects.

title: G7 agrees coordinated export controls on advanced chip-making tools
summary: Members committed to harmonise restrictions on deep-UV lithography equipment after months of negotiation. The measure is aimed at preserving semiconductor leads without triggering retaliation.

title: Mohsin Hamid returns with a novel about borders and belonging
summary: The author of Exit West has written a shorter, stranger book set in an unnamed city where citizens disappear overnight. Early reviews call it his most politically urgent work yet.

title: How Urdu literature is finding new readers through translated podcasts
summary: A Lahore-based production house is turning Manto short stories into audio dramas with full translation. The series has attracted half a million listeners outside South Asia within its first month.

title: Apple redesigns system fonts for variable display sizes in iOS 19
summary: The new typeface scales letter spacing and weight dynamically across screen sizes and ambient light conditions. Accessibility advocates say it reduces eye strain for users with low vision.

title: Bitcoin tops $110,000 as sovereign wealth funds accumulate
summary: Three government-linked investment vehicles disclosed positions totalling 0.4 percent of circulating supply. Analysts expect institutional demand to remain firm ahead of the next halving.

title: Pakistan pilots RAAST cross-border transfer with UAE
summary: A real-time link between the two countries instant payment systems went live in a trial with five banks. The corridor is designed to lower remittance costs from the Pakistani diaspora in the UAE.

title: HEC reports 20 percent rise in Pakistani students studying abroad on scholarships
summary: The Higher Education Commission funded 4,200 scholarships this cycle, up from 3,500 last year. STEM and medicine account for 65 percent of placements.

title: Gilgit-Baltistan tops budget travel lists for third year running
summary: Adventure travel platforms cite improved road access, new guesthouses and competitive trekking packages as key drivers. The tourism board is targeting a million visitors by 2026.

title: Coke Studio Season 16 breaks streaming record with opening episode
summary: The premiere episode crossed 10 million YouTube views in 24 hours, surpassing all previous seasons. A collaboration between a Lahore rapper and a classical singer drew the most attention.
